commit.message:
merge: lazy git-server fetch in pr commands, with expanded scope

Original contribution from m0wer
(nostr:npub1w3vaxva0vcrx7pnvlpmede5smvafdl69xnu7ma82kaxl9us89zdsht4c5c):
`ngit pr list` / `pr apply` / `pr checkout` were calling
`git fetch <nostr-remote>` as a subprocess, which would also trigger
fetches against unrelated remotes configured in `.git/config`
(GitHub, Codeberg, …), prompting for SSH keys the user hadn't opted
into. The fetch is unnecessary for PR operations — these commands only
need fresh nostr event data — so the subprocess call is replaced with
`fetching_with_report` against nostr relays only, matching the pattern
already used by `ngit sync`, `issue list`, `pr_status`, etc.

Expanded scope added during review:

- `checkout_patch` best-effort-fetches the patch chain's parent commit
  from the repo's git servers before `apply_patch_chain`, restoring
  the "newer revision based on a commit we haven't pulled yet" path
  that the original commit broke for patch-kind proposals.

- The three duplicated `fetch_oid_for_*_pr` helpers in apply.rs /
  checkout.rs / list.rs are consolidated into a single
  `ensure_commit_local` in `src/lib/fetch.rs` that short-circuits on
  `does_commit_exist` before any network call.

- `ngit pr checkout` (both the no-branch-yet case and the --force
  diverged case) and the interactive checkout path in `ngit pr list`
  now try the submitter-supplied `clone`-tag URLs on the PR event as a
  fallback if the repo's declared git servers don't carry the PR tip,
  matching what `ngit pr apply` already did. The same fallback remains
  deliberately disabled for the passive `git clone` / `git fetch` paths
  in the remote helper, where a malicious submitter could otherwise
  slow down every operation against the repo.

- `ngit pr checkout` now writes `refs/remotes/<nostr-remote>/<branch>`
  to the verified locally-applied tip and sets the branch's upstream on
  every successful checkout, so `git pull` works against the nostr
  remote afterwards. The tracking ref is written from the deterministic
  OID produced by `create_commit_from_patch` rather than a subprocess
  `git fetch <nostr-remote>` (which would have re-introduced the very
  auth-prompt regression this PR set out to fix). Applies to both
  PR-kind and patch-kind proposals; the interactive `ngit pr list`
  PR-kind arm is migrated and the patch-kind interactive arms are
  deferred to a follow-up (TODO marker in list.rs).

commit.message:
fix(pr): restore tracking-branch UX on pr checkout

`ngit pr checkout` now writes `refs/remotes/<nostr-remote>/<branch>` to
the verified locally-applied tip and sets the branch's upstream to that
remote on every successful checkout, so `git pull` works against the
nostr remote afterwards. Applies to both PR-kind and patch-kind
proposals. The tracking ref is written from the deterministic OID
produced by `create_commit_from_patch` rather than a subprocess
`git fetch <nostr-remote>` (which would otherwise prompt for auth on
unrelated remotes). Restores the UX lost in 554a7e8.

Also drops the defer-to-`git pull` short-circuit in `checkout_pr` that
fired whenever the branch already had an upstream set: with universal
tracking it would fire every time and hide the behind / diverged /
force paths the command is meant to drive. The three FIXMEs in
`tests/pr_checkout.rs` explicitly flagged this as a bug; those tests
are un-ignored.

The interactive `ngit pr list` PR-kind arm is migrated; the patch-kind
interactive arms are deferred to a follow-up (TODO marker added in
list.rs).

The newer-revision PR-kind test now publishes the revision as the
maintainer rather than a fresh contributor — mirroring the patch-kind
sibling — so the `PR_UPDATE` event passes the `permissioned_users`
filter in `get_all_proposal_patch_pr_pr_update_events_from_cache`
and the second `ngit pr checkout` actually sees the revision in the
candidate set.

commit.message:
feat(pr): trust PR clone-tag URLs in pr checkout / list-interactive

ngit pr apply already tried the submitter-supplied git-server URLs from
the PR event's `clone` tags as a fallback if the repo's declared
servers didn't carry the PR tip. pr checkout (both the no-branch-yet
case and the --force diverged case) and the interactive checkout path
in pr list did not, even though all three are explicit user-targeted
actions on a specific PR.

The asymmetry was conservative but unnecessary: the DoS concern that
keeps clone-tag URLs out of the trust set in the remote helper is
specifically about passive fan-out — `git clone` / `git fetch`
iterating every open PR and getting blocked by one slow submitter-
controlled server. When the user has typed `ngit pr checkout <id>`
they have already opted into that single PR; trying the submitter's
hint as a fallback to the repo's declared servers is the same
trade-off pr apply already makes.

Extract the URL-extraction helper to `git_events::pr_event_clone_tag_urls`
(with a doc-comment spelling out when it is safe to use), drop the local
copy in apply.rs, and pass it as `extras_to_try_first` from the three
PR-checkout sites.

commit.message:
fix(pr): fetch patch parent from git servers when missing in pr checkout

After commit 554a7e8 removed the implicit `git fetch <nostr-remote>` from
ngit pr sub-commands, `ngit pr checkout` on a patch-kind proposal whose
parent commit was not yet present locally failed with `failed to find
parent commit (...). run git pull and try again.` This is exactly the
"newer revision based on a commit we haven't pulled yet" case, hit by
tests/pr_checkout_patch.rs::newer_revision_force_updates_to_revised_tip.

checkout_patch now best-effort-fetches the patch chain's parent commit
(via `get_parent_commit_from_patch` on the oldest patch in the chain)
from the repo's git servers before each `apply_patch_chain` call. The
fetch is a no-op when the commit is already local, so the common case
pays no network cost.

While here, extract the duplicated fetch_oid_for_*_pr helpers from
apply.rs, checkout.rs and list.rs into a single `ensure_commit_local`
in src/lib/fetch.rs. The shared helper short-circuits on
does_commit_exist before any network call (previously only apply.rs
guarded its call site; checkout.rs and list.rs entered the fetch loop
unconditionally and only checked at the end of the loop in order to
bail with an error). Net behaviour change for checkout/list: fewer
git-server roundtrips when the commit is already present.

commit.message:
fix(pr): avoid fetching from non-nostr git remotes in pr commands

ngit pr list, pr apply, and pr checkout were calling `git fetch
<nostr-remote>` as a subprocess. When git processes this fetch, it
can also trigger fetches from other remotes configured in .git/config
(e.g. GitHub, Codeberg). These fetches are unnecessary for PR
operations and inconvenient when those remotes require SSH keys.

These commands only need to refresh nostr event data (proposals,
patches, statuses). Replace the subprocess `git fetch` call with
`fetching_with_report` which fetches only from nostr relays, matching
the pattern used by ngit sync, issue list, pr_status, and other
sub-commands.

Git objects (commits) for PR checkout/apply are still fetched from
the nostr-registered git servers via fetch_from_git_server when
actually needed (i.e., when the tip commit is not yet available
locally).

commit.message:
fix(checkout): pr checkout left working directory at previous state

The previous checkout_remote_branch_with_tracking called set_head then
checkout_head(None). After set_head moves HEAD to the new branch,
libgit2's GIT_CHECKOUT_SAFE treats the workdir files (still matching
the old branch) as modified relative to the new baseline and refuses
to update them, leaving the index and workdir at the old tree.

Fix: call checkout_tree(commit, None) first, then set_head — matching
the order used by Repo::checkout() in src/lib/git/mod.rs.

GIT_CHECKOUT_SAFE preserves untracked files, ignored files, staged
changes, and workdir modifications to files that differ between the
old and new trees, so no user work is lost.

Also removes the #[ignore] from the revision scenario in
tests/pr_checkout_patch.rs which was blocked on this bug. The test
is updated to use the maintainer clone for the revision (so patches
pass the permissioned_users filter) and to push the rebase-base
commit before ngit send so apply_patch_chain can find the parent.

commit.message:
merge branch 'pr/test-harness-replacement'

nostr:nevent1qvzqqqqx2gpzpgqgmmc409hm4xsdd74sf68a2uyf9pwel4g9mfdg8l5244t6x4jdqy88wumn8ghj7mn0wvhxcmmv9uq3camnwvaz7tmwva5hgtnyv9hxxmmwwashjer9wchxxmmd9uqzqnkzcj3je0ncs0kf7krazh0n3g4r0suk78meyz4vvpzde55p75ayp69rkt

From PR description:

Completely replaces the integration test harness
(`test_utils/` → `test_harness/`) and rewrites every integration test
against it. Parallel-by-default, no global state, no #[serial],
no PTY/rexpect, no exact-stdout assertions.

This is the fourth attempt. The previous three stalled because the
rewrite was big enough that main always got ahead of the branch
before it landed. Merging now — even with known gaps — is the point:
the old harness is a blocker for further planned improvements, and
"perfect" has lost three times already.

Known follow-ups (intentionally not blocking):

- git push pr/<branch> push-side auto-detection is untested.
Pre-existing gap, not a regression — captured here so it's not
forgotten when the default flips from patches to PRs.

- --password / ncryptsec storage has no coverage anywhere. Lighthouse
test to be written against the then-current contract if it ever breaks.
Raw git-remote-nostr protocol layer (the old CLI-tester pattern driving
 list/fetch/push commands directly) is replaced by end-to-end git
 command testing. Deliberate scope reduction.

- ~13 single-test files could be consolidated with OnceCell shared
fixtures for a marginal CI speedup. Low priority — real per-test cost
is grasp subprocess startup, not Cargo binary scheduling.

- One incidental production fix landed alongside (NIP-21 q tag for hex
event ids in EventRefType::Quote; previously hex and bech32 produced
different tags for the same logical reference). Tests pin both paths.

Design: docs/architecture/test-harness.md. Rules every new test must
follow: AGENTS.md § "Test harness boundary".
